## Candidate status

This document describes an authored integration candidate. The new family names, canonical resources, scope routing, builder inputs and source inventory have not yet been generated, compiled or qualified together. Historical component results from a733 and main do not qualify this new source.

The immutable inputs are main `51bc24b8b03e5adc3da1b2b3490ad5cc7357e8d8` and a733 `a733926a2786a3d4a37304bd2d18ebb2eac57ac9`. The original main document remains at `docs/HIA_CORE_EMITTER_NATIVE.md`. The original a733 document is recoverable verbatim at that path in the fixed a733 commit; its old selector names must not be used as aliases for this family.

## Explicit selection

| Item | CONTROL value |
| --- | --- |
| Selector | `HEPTA_HIA_CORE_EMITTER_CONTROL_MANIFEST` |
| Manifest schema | `hepta.hia.core-emitter-control-native.v1` |
| HIA source | `examples/hia_bootstrap/core_emitter.hepta` |
| Native module | `hepta.hia_core_emitter_control_native` |
| Selection module | `hepta.hia_core_emitter_control_selection` |
| Generator | `tools.generate_hia_core_emitter_control` |
| Builder | `tools.build_hia_core_emitter_control` |

The main family retains its pool plus eight units, checked ABI, worker scheduling and in-process continuation execution. CONTROL uses one image containing all six original `_Emitter` methods and their lazy policy. Main and CONTROL have different constructor/continuation ABIs and are never substituted for each other.

The existing main selector `HEPTA_HIA_CORE_EMITTER_MANIFEST` keeps its original ABI. Selecting it together with the CONTROL selector is rejected before either manifest or image is admitted. A complete public operation captures the selected family, or explicit absence, once. Callback changes to environment selectors cannot silently switch the active implementation. A selected failure is returned as a failure; it does not enter the other family or the retained reference.

## Reproduction requirements

The canonical source must be regenerated in the actual combined source checkout. A build must use that exact source's current completed cold report and compiler. The existing compiler, cold, group and whole-suite limits are unchanged. An old image, old cold report or source-only result is not a substitute.

```sh
python -m tools.generate_hia_core_emitter_control
python -m tools.build_hia_core_emitter_control --output NEW_DIRECTORY --compiler CURRENT_B3 --cold-report CURRENT_COLD_REPORT
```

Source selector: `tests.test_hia_core_emitter_control_native.CoreEmitterSourceTests`.
Native selector: `tests.test_hia_core_emitter_control_native.CoreEmitterNativeTests`.
Caller entry: `tools.qualify_hia_core_emitter_control_callers`; retain its original arguments and complete caller groups.

The caller qualifier retains all 15 CONTROL component methods and the original complete 51- and 50-method caller groups. The original main qualifier and its original component module remain separate.

The main original suites, CONTROL full-frame/VM tests, installed-wheel controls, changed-source/image rejection, actual observer counts, exception identities and operand-retirement observations all remain required. Installed fixtures include all eleven original main resource groups.

The selected HIA program owns its reviewed policy. Python remains the fixed object/FFI transport and supplies the original external providers. # HIA-owned program Emitter candidate

The complete original six-method `_Emitter` policy is compiled to nine `.hepta`
units: one typed literal owner and eight 64-instruction continuation units.
`HEPTA_HIA_CORE_EMITTER_MANIFEST` is explicit opt-in, with a distinct bundle,
unit and ABI schema. Every package source, ABI, manifest and image is bound.
The ordinary emitter captures one selection for the complete operation.
Subclasses and unselected calls retain their original behavior.

The original policy AST is retained independently in the pinned `608` fixture.
The authoring adapter transports the five constructor arguments in one exact
tuple, preserving the four-bound-argument packet limit. Sole keyword mapping
calls, four-value unpacking, relative import lookup and lazy item projection
use explicit generic hosted object-runtime helpers. Lazy projection is not
replaced by eager materialization: partial `list.extend` writes and exception
ordering remain observable. Unsupported grammar fails authoring.

This candidate does **not** replace the Python object runtime, callable and
iterator plumbing, Core verifier, native byte wrapper, ELF writer, image loader,
filesystem, worker persistence, build orchestration or installation handoff.
The generic 18 object packet opcodes and four additional mechanical callable
helpers remain hosted. Core `_Function` lowering is a separate admitted bundle;
tests must distinguish Emitter-only selection from paired selection. Neither
selection enables itself by default or authorizes legacy retirement.

Development compilation may explicitly reuse an older qualified compiler;
that is not matching-source cold acceptance. Exact source regeneration, own
cold replay, all native gates, full regression and independent source/installed
replays remain required before integrating this candidate.


## Development observations (not formal acceptance)

The nine current HIA units were actually compiled with explicit reuse of the
v80 source compiler. The complete Emitter development gate executed all 110
planned tests (9 component, 51 original machine and 50 original Core), zero
anomalies, in 109.44 seconds under the original 180-second owner. All six Emitter
modes had actual admitted native step returns, all source and image identities
were stable, and retained Emitter methods were forbidden for original callers.
The installed wheel ran isolated without site packages, authoring imports or
PATH tools. This does not admit current-source cold identity. A separate paired
Emitter/Function run remains required; its complete source and image pins must
be retained separately from this single-owner observation.


The separate paired development run also executed all 110 tests, zero anomalies,
in 137.14 seconds (137.29-second original process owner, limit 180). Both the
Emitter and independent Function bundles were source/image pinned before and
after. The original machine and Core groups returned actual native Function
steps, while all original Emitter/Function bodies and five scoped helper bodies
were forbidden. This remains explicit development-only compiler/bundle reuse,
not current-source cold acceptance or default whole-stack activation.


## Import callback correction (successor, not inherited acceptance)

A read-only diagnostic on frozen v81 found that its importlib-based bridge
bypassed the original `__import__` hook. Existing source, native and installed
results remain scoped historical observations, not complete equivalence. Its
unstarted full queue was retired without modifying v81 or interrupting v80's
actual full run. The successor uses a fixed mechanical CPython import opcode
template with the original module globals, retaining hook parameters,
IMPORT_FROM attribute fallback and ImportError behavior. This is still hosted
object-runtime machinery, not HIA or Python-runtime retirement. Two added
native regressions exercise actual HIA constructor import success/refusal and
foreign import-from result/error observation. Current HIA source bytes are
unchanged; current-source cold and full acceptance are not inherited.


The corrected import successor completed all 112 paired development tests
(11 component, 51 original machine, 50 original Core), zero anomalies, in
166.11 seconds. Original 180-second owner completed naturally in
166.22 seconds. The new import regressions, actual isolated wheel,
all six native Emitter modes and both real Function caller groups passed;
complete source and both admitted bundles remained stable. This is still
explicit development reuse, not successor matching-source cold acceptance.

# General Core function lowering: development work in progress

This branch holds an unqualified authoring candidate for moving the complete
`_Function` policy in `hepta.hia_program_native` into HIA. It is not integrated
into the ordinary product entry. The first actual authoring run checked the
original 22 methods and five helpers, then generated one literal-pool unit before
the first control unit failed the unchanged Core type verifier. Revision 3
corrects only the internal helper return types and remains unexecuted.
No native compilation, Core VM, component/caller result, installed owner or
matching-source cold qualification exists for this Core candidate.

## Exact source and proposed boundary

The independent base is commit
`608157e52b0b94e0d294f6b99c4e809869f183aa`, tree
`e7c29a60796a1a78946a2c667aa80df86529e532`.
The complete original 47,839-byte module is retained at
the `tests/fixtures` directory, named `hia_program_native_608.py.txt`, as the independent oracle.

The proposed owner is all 22 `_Function` methods and the five helpers
`_reject`, `_words`, `_bounds`, `_normalize`, and `_prologue`.
It includes frame and slot assignment, edge/call staging, register versus slot
selection, all 50 currently supported Core opcode branches, range and allocation
control, chains, block and terminator order, trap emission, and function reports.

The authoring policy is copied from that exact source; a restricted authoring
compiler lowers its control into explicit continuation instructions. The later
generator is intended to render those instructions as HIA. Unsupported syntax
must refuse generation. Runtime must not execute or import this authoring policy,
compiler, or oracle. This is a source-translation design, not a table of
precomputed program outputs.

The original `_Emitter` module policy, verifier, machine-plan provider, wrapper
construction, native Code primitives, ELF writer, linker, filesystem operations,
and arbitrary object effects remain outside this proposed owner. Code state,
encoding, and ELF are independently owned work and are not modified here.

## Intended observation discipline

HIA will choose every control branch and the order of individual primitive
observations: attribute/item binding, calls, iteration, truth and rich comparison,
arithmetic, packing, and writes. Actual Python objects and their foreign hooks
remain observations, including independent `__ne__`, evaluation order, exceptions,
and reentrant effects. A mere Python wrapper around the former lowering decisions
would not satisfy this scope.

A source-bound explicit selector, immutable selection scope, versioned one-shot
continuation protocol, and finite HIA unit split are planned. The existing
compiler limits, 64 KiB frame limit, 16 MiB text limit, original caller
denominators, and 3/5-second product budgets must remain unchanged. No performance,
ABI, lifetime, or foreign-domain equivalence claim is established by this static
checkpoint.

## Custody and execution status

The local executor became unavailable during a write. Its last filesystem
mutation acknowledgement is unknown. These files were recovered from retained
tool-call text and the canonical original module, then saved through Git APIs.
The earlier policy reconstruction matches its observed 21,778-byte size, but its
original local hash is unavailable. It is explicitly not presented as a
byte-verified restoration of that local file.

The current candidate additionally uses the original frozenset kind for
`BYTE_RESOURCES`, and refuses a reducer shape lacking an explicit default.
These are new static edits. The earlier requested source text is retained
separately under `experiments/hia_core_lowering_20261111/static-wip-r1`; no prior observation is relabelled.

The first remote authoring request was never dispatched. The corrected r2
request ran once on the pinned CPython 3.14.4 executable, with the original
180-second guardian. All four new Python files passed syntax checks; the complete
22-method class and five helper ASTs matched the retained oracle. It compiled
28 modes into 1,922 control instructions with at most 510 object slots.
The complete 3,925-leaf base and 3,936-leaf candidate byte/mode inventories
matched before and after the attempt.

Of 32 planned HIA units, the literal pool passed the public Core roundtrip.
The first control unit failed with `E_HIA_TYPE` because a `u32` helper result
was compared to a `u64` literal. The run finished HOLD after 22.007921965 seconds;
the guardian naturally reaped the leader and observed ECHILD without timeout or
live-child killing. The original report and logs are preserved in commit
55e39d6a65ff848ee7596c548ddbf98e391bcbdf under the remote-authoring-r2 terminal
directory. No native compiler or product test ran in that remote request.

Separately, seven earlier pushes to this development branch triggered the old
GitHub workflow. Those runs failed and are not native qualifications. In the
latest run, 43085426169 at exact head 55e39d6, the source job rejected a document
reference and the cold command rejected source-closure drift before writing a
cold report. Its job logs and exact run identities are preserved separately.
Future evidence and unexecuted source checkpoints use `[skip ci]`.

## Static revision 2

The renderer emits HIA control units with 64 finite control instructions per
unit, and a separate HIA-owned typed literal pool. The HIA program chooses
cross-unit handoffs using its own program counter. The bridge decodes only the
versioned literal framing and primitive requests. It binds all 22 original
method signatures to native invocations; the ordinary product selector and
source-bound loader have not yet been added.

The 128-byte request/acknowledgement protocol carries a sequence, phase, mode,
object handles and raw truth/iteration observations. Private state remains HIA
owned. Foreign permission is consumed before the effect; BaseException in a
native step, post-call framing or foreign effect permanently closes the session.
No claim about that protocol is validated by this unexecuted source.

The intended initial domain retains normal module and built-in bindings.
Monkeypatching the five private helpers or the reducer built-ins is not silently
presented as equivalent: helper names always select their HIA implementations,
and sum/max/any generator control is compiled into HIA. Literal object identity,
arbitrary stack/traceback introspection, foreign finalizer timing, recursive
resource exhaustion, and tampering with private registries are also unproven.
Normal public method argument binding, dynamic receiver attributes, independent
rich comparisons, module value observations and actual Code effects remain
explicit compatibility targets. Remaining limits must be reported rather than
removed by an implicit retained-owner fallback.

Source revision 2 also refuses value-context chained comparisons, which are
absent from the current policy, rather than incorrectly normalizing arbitrary
rich comparison results into booleans. Original source and all prior unknown
write records remain unchanged in history.

## Revision 3 type correction

Internal startup, instruction-group and dispatch helpers now return `u64`,
matching the existing word-sized status comparisons. The public lowering and
literal-pool entries still return `u32`. Every defined internal status remains
one of 0, 1, 2, 4 or the unchanged ABI refusal value; the final entry conversion
does not add an admitted status. This is an authoring type correction, not a
change to the verifier, compiler caps, packet, phase sequence or policy IR.
The corrected ca871 source was generated once on the pinned desktop CPython 3.14.4:
all 32 public Core roundtrips and all original caps passed in 65.0857341099 seconds.
The original 3,925-leaf base and 3,937-leaf candidate stayed byte/mode identical.
The guardian naturally reaped the process and observed ECHILD; it did not time out
or kill a live child. Compact raw results are preserved in 9efc2fb. No native
compiler, VM or product test ran in that source-only request. The original failing
source and the first unknown local write remain preserved.


## Ordinary entry integration draft

The new integration source is a separate, unexecuted revision. It does not
inherit a native or product pass from the source-only r3 run. The explicit
environment selector is HEPTA_HIA_CORE_LOWERING_MANIFEST. The ordinary backend
entry captures either its admitted 32-image bundle or the absence of a selection
for the entire emit, including reentrant emission. Subclasses of the retained
private Function class keep their existing behavior.

The five shared helpers use the selected HIA owner within that captured scope.
Outside it their earlier public-admission and target-error behavior remains
hosted. Direct selected Function invocations resolve their five helpers through
the HIA owner. The original 22 method bodies and five helper bodies remain
separately available for AST and semantic comparison; a selected load failure
does not call them.

The loader reads the installed ABI, every HIA unit source and every unit manifest
on selection. It binds one compiler identity across all 32 images and caches
immutable mappings as a complete bundle. The backend implementation identity
also binds both new Python bridge modules, the ABI, all 32 source hashes, the
bundle hash and all actual image hashes. A changed unit-manifest key requires
fresh image admission. An unchanged warm key retains its already immutable
mapping; changing a disk image alone does not rewrite that mapping.

The strict builder requires a successful matching-source cold report before
creating its output directory. Development use of the old 0e09 compiler is
separate and cannot authorize that production builder. The new component gate
declares four source methods and eight native methods. The caller gate keeps the
original five machine modules and their 51 identifiers, plus the four existing
general Core modules and their 50 identifiers. All loaded and executed
identifiers must match, with zero errors, failures, skips, expected failures or
unexpected successes. No existing test or original time limit is changed.

The installed control builds a real wheel, compares every installed Python file
and declared resource, and invokes ordinary emission in an isolated child with
no site initialization, empty PATH and an authoring-import refusal. These are
unexecuted controls until a new result explicitly records their actual execution.

The 18 primitive kinds remain hosted observations, including object allocation
and storage, arbitrary precision arithmetic, interpreter builtins and actual Code
methods. Python generator objects are not created for HIA reductions; arbitrary
foreign StopIteration/PEP479 behavior and monkeypatching reducer builtins are not
included in the ordinary verified-builtin claim. The existing arbitrary
recursion/resource, finalizer and introspection limitations also remain.
No retained implementation is removed and no default selection is enabled.

## Instruction owner integration boundary

The ordinary-entry draft additionally preserves the exact 7186dee24f33173c25f2246a6dfe15eeda053992 machine-state and instruction-control source. The backend identity includes hia_machine_state_native.py, hia_machine_instructions_native.py and hia_json_wire_native.py alongside both Core-lowering bridges. The existing native_encoding_scope implementation and its independently selected Code owners remain unchanged. The complete original Function and helper oracle is still the exact 608 source; these bodies did not change in 7186. This source merge does not inherit native/caller qualification for the new composition. Its private v72 contract definition still requires actual regeneration and source-bound validation before any cold-built claim.

## Original-source recovery and execution accounting

The 32 original r3 HIA files were recovered from the same e86 custody archive:
2,218,343 compressed bytes with SHA256
400f59e67817fb9a6fc3ce744b4bb93c64957d932272880af7bb382325a2c450.
All 58 members were independently checked against their original byte, size,
mode and uid/gid records. The 32 source files total 5,546,188 bytes and were
published without regeneration in 028058563592a853c7b4eeea145b35f5545aaa94.
The original read timeouts, partial transfers and subsequent complete recovery
remain in that commit's custody history. This establishes source custody only.

The selected-caller producer distinguishes invocation attempts from ordinary
method returns and actual native step returns. Its native_step_returns ledger
records the group, original mode and mode number, actual control-unit index,
unit name, admitted image, ABI and bundle digests, returned status and count.
A row is added only after LoweringSession.step completes the actual HIA entry
and admits its output frame. Status1 can request a later rejection primitive;
it is not a claim that the method or product succeeded. The original _reject
method therefore need not return normally. All 27 public policy modes must have
actual native step returns across the complete 12 + 51 + 50 run, and each of its
three groups must have actual returns. The unchanged 28th private diagnostic
mode is outside that 27-mode requirement.

Control-unit index 0 denotes core_lowering_000. The complete bundle includes the
literal pool at bundle index 0, so a control unit's bundle_image_index is its
unit_index plus 1. All 32 source/image bindings remain independently admitted,
including the pool.

The producer separately retains before/after original bytes for the caller
bundle and the component's fresh qualified bundle. It captures the latter after
unittest has performed its one real setUpClass, before the first method, without
calling setup again. Cold mode requires both actual build.json receipts and
both sets of 32 images/manifests. The original machine and general Core groups
use the caller bundle. Development mode is explicitly separate and may reuse
the selected development bundle for the component; it never claims a fresh
cold build. These revised producer controls have not yet been executed.

### Development phase isolation

The caller driver accepts `--development-group component|original-machine|original-core` only with an explicit development manifest. A supplied cold report rejects that option before creating output. The selected group still loads and executes its entire original 12, 51, or 50 method set, preserves all five anomaly refusals, and records the same native return and input-identity observations. Its successful status is `DEVELOPMENT_GROUP_PASS`, its scope is `EXPLICIT_DEVELOPMENT_GROUP_ONLY`, and it explicitly does not claim complete three-group qualification. This permits three independent process owners with the original 180-second boundary each. A separate development aggregate must bind all three reports to the same candidate and original compiled bundle, require all 113 original methods and the 27 public modes in the union of actual native returns, and preserve every phase's original receipt. The ordinary default and cold invocation still require all three groups in one report and retain their existing complete-coverage requirements.

The ABI contains 28 modes: 22 `_Function` methods, five shared helpers, and the independent `_native_globals` fixture mode. The 27 public product control modes remain the required cross-group union. The existing component literal-owner method separately invokes mode 28 and compares its entire returned structure with the original constants; the component and complete reports additionally require its actual HIA step-return observation. It is not silently removed from the ABI or relabeled as an ordinary product call.

## Current integration candidate

This independently identified successor composes the selected Core owner with the admitted machine encoding/state/instruction and machine-plan boundaries. The original Function methods and helper ASTs remain unchanged. ELF selection is deliberately not imported from the incomplete upstream ELF candidate. Sources use `.hepta`. This composition has not yet passed its own source/native/cold/caller qualification. Hosted object primitives, default activation, the Emitter, runtime and whole-product retirement remain open.

### Current candidate development observations

The 32 checked-in HIA units were actually regenerated with the original 180-second process owner, then compiled using an explicitly reused older-source v78 compiler. This is development construction, not current-source cold admission. The complete three-group development producer passed all 12 component, 51 original machine and 50 original Core methods (113 total), with all five anomaly lists empty and the original methods unchanged. The external original 180-second owner completed naturally in 136.673636510 seconds. All 27 public modes had actual admitted HIA step returns; the private literal-owner mode was also observed. The report distinguishes invocation attempts, admitted native step returns and ordinary method success. The original Function/helper owners were forbidden in selected ordinary calls.

These observations do not qualify the new source closure, default activation, the Emitter, arbitrary Python primitive execution or the whole product. A separate frozen source, own cold replay, exact native workflow and retained full regression remain required. Original upstream WIP and failure observations above are retained as history, not relabelled as passes.

### Resource classification correction

The first frozen integration source gate actually executed all 505 methods and failed two existing resource checks: ABI data under `hepta/` did not satisfy the bootstrap inventory partition, and the single-image runtime bridge catalog could not classify a multi-image compiler bundle. That candidate remains frozen with its original failure logs.

This successor moves the unchanged ABI bytes to `docs/HIA_CORE_LOWERING_ABI.json`, registers that ABI and the 32 backend compiler sources under the separate `BACKEND_BUILD_FILES` role, and retains the original single-image `NATIVE_SOURCE_FILES` contract. Both lists remain explicit, disjoint and fully installed. The runtime reads the same canonical package-owned resource path that the compiler builder and backend identity bind. No original assertion, denominator or admission guard is changed. Fresh qualification is required.

The original one-entry `COMPILER_BUILD_FILES` and three-entry `SOURCE_BUILD_FILES` assertions remain unchanged. A new exact backend-role assertion cross-checks all 32 sources against the actual installed ABI; all prior completeness, disjointness, identity and no-fallback checks remain. Wheel source fixtures copy this additional role as well. An initial development attempt put these inputs in the closed compiler role and was correctly rejected; that failed log is retained.

The corrected source-development check passed all 16 targeted resource, source-closure and Core-source methods. Independent AST comparison retained every original assertion across all 23 resource-fixture files, with added exact backend-role coverage. The first stale-contract/closed-role development failures remain retained; fresh full source, cold and native gates are still required for this successor.

# Native HIA machine-plan validation and register witnesses

The selected owner in `examples/hia_bootstrap/machine_plan.hepta` implements
the finite block-layout v1 and machine-plan v2/v3/v4 admission rules and the
closed-block scalar register witness. It is connected to the ordinary public
`validate_plan` and `register_assignment_witness` entrypoints through the explicit
`HEPTA_HIA_MACHINE_PLAN_MANIFEST` selection. A selected failure never calls a
retained plan implementation.

This is one native responsibility in the retained product. It does not replace
the complete backend, the Python object ABI, or the ordinary Core verifier.

## Responsibilities

HIA owns the schema and exact field sets, Core identity comparison, complete
block/function permutations, scratch-register bijection, finite instruction
choices, alignment and scalar-select admission. It determines every normal
exact-string function/SSA membership decision, scalar/leaf eligibility,
definition and last-use position, inclusive interval collision, first-refusal
order and witness ordering. A dead definition still occupies its write point.
Block parameters and terminator uses retain their ordinary lifetime rules.
Collisions are checked before observing mappings for a later block.

Function and block permutations use merge sorting. A sorted SSA index and binary
search avoid input-dependent hash collision costs inside HIA. Register witnesses
are ordered by original block order and value spelling; interference is checked
by block, admitted register order, first position and value spelling. The v4
caller-clobbered registers retain the exact finite leaf opcode/signature gate.

The host bridge transports the already verified immutable Core, retains the
original bounded plain-JSON plan capture, and materializes HIA-selected results.
It does not compute liveness, classify opcodes, choose accepted schemas or call
either retained semantic owner. The source-order public witness hook is still
called with the detached plan. A context-local captured image keeps that hook
on the same selected owner even if caller code changes the environment.

## Foreign object observations

The standalone witness API accepts a Python truth-conversion object for its
leaf-register flag. Such a callback can mutate an otherwise exact input
dictionary. HIA therefore drives observation stages instead of assuming that
the first map read is a snapshot of all later reads:

1. Check every initial outer function name, then perform the first truth
   conversion.
2. For each observed mapping, check its complete exact-kind/register gate before
   looking up its function in the retained immutable Core object dictionary.
3. Observe fresh leaf-register membership and execute HIA leaf/SSA gates. HIA
   requests generic dictionary membership/lookup only when a foreign key needs
   Python hash/equality semantics. Exact Core identifiers use its own SSA index.
4. In block/value order, observe membership and both original dictionary reads
   separately. An opaque handle preserves the first observed register object;
   the second lookup supplies the native-selected register bucket. HIA checks
   each block's complete interference before advancing to the next block.
5. Observe callee-register membership, materialize HIA-selected intervals,
   insert the result under the original foreign function key, and only then
   perform the second truth conversion. The optional result update performs
   the original dictionary lookup again.

These callbacks are mechanical foreign object operations. They retain actual
`KeyError`, `TypeError`, user hash/equality/truth conversion and dictionary
mutation behavior at the original boundaries. The adapter does not replace a
native refusal with hosted validation. Private buffers are per invocation;
reentrant or concurrent calls share only immutable executable code.

## Custody and execution limits

The local manifest schema is `hepta.hia.machine-plan-native.v1`. It binds the
package-owned HIA source, immutable native image and compiler image digests.
Every selection rereads the manifest and current source, including a warm code
cache. The emitting backend's implementation hash additionally binds the new
bridge/transport code and selected source/image identity; it rechecks that
identity before publishing an artifact.

The native entry uses the existing three-buffer Linux x86-64 LP64 ABI. It has
private request/state words, bounded typed transport and checked output offsets.
The state buffer grows from actual captured plan/Core transport sizes. Four
merge arrays plus 64-byte rows consume 96 bytes per SSA definition, below the
reserved multiple of the actual immutable Core transport. Plan permutations
reserve 24 bytes per member. No smaller block, function, node or byte allowance
is silently imposed on the existing verified Core profile.

The adapter's Core custody precondition remains an already verified immutable
Core. Bounded JSON capture, foreign Python operations, source/manifest custody,
object materialization, static `code_options`/`preservation_checks`, machine
encoding, linking and publication still have retained host responsibilities.
The native image is locally selected trusted executable code, not a sandbox or
an all-input refinement proof.

## Build and qualification

`python -B -m tools.build_hia_machine_plan --compiler <image> --cold-report
<report> --output <new-directory>` uses the shared complete current-source cold
gate. The machine-plan source must be in that complete contract. An old compiler
with identical image bytes does not authorize changed source, and unqualified
input creates no artifact directory.

`tests.test_hia_machine_plan_native` checks independent ordinary Core VM
execution, source reproduction, exact retained-oracle custody, refusal priority,
foreign mutation order, immutable plan/owner capture, warm source admission and
backend identity. Native tests require an explicit
`HEPTA_HIA_MACHINE_PLAN_COLD_REPORT` or a distinctly named
`HEPTA_HIA_MACHINE_PLAN_DEVELOPMENT_MANIFEST`; the two cannot override each other.
An actual wheel build/install control executes the public selected entrypoints
from the installed package under `-I -S -B`, with an empty `PATH`, authoring
imports forbidden and both retained plan owners forbidden. Changed or missing
installed source is refused even after the native code cache is warm. Setting
`HEPTA_HIA_MACHINE_PLAN_FIXTURE_EVIDENCE` to a new directory retains the complete
fixture, wheel, child program, process arguments and original output streams;
ordinary test execution uses a cleaned temporary directory.

`tools/qualify_hia_machine_plan_native_callers.py` runs the unchanged original
machine-plan, scalar-register, leaf-register and Agent machine-choice suites.
Both retained plan owners are forbidden. The report records loaded and executed
test IDs, every unittest anomaly, actual native entry counts, source/manifest
readbacks and native image identity. Cold qualification permits no exclusions.
Development observations are explicitly labelled and cannot qualify a release.
The optional `--evidence-dir` names a new create-only directory that retains
the actual cold-built caller image and manifest, including partial files after
a failure. The workflow and full qualification runner supply this directory
and preserve it with the original report. An externally selected development
bundle is referenced rather than copied by this option.

The original draft's foreign-flag counterexamples and an initial test-fixture
failure are preserved separately from corrected executions. Full product
replacement, default activation and retirement of retained implementations are
not implied by the selected component or its development tests.

"""Explicit selection between reviewed bundle and single-image Core families.

The original selectors keep their bundle and in-process scheduling protocols.
The CONTROL selectors name independent single-image ABIs. Both selectors for
one owner are rejected before admission; a captured selection, including None,
cannot be replaced by a later callback. This module performs no backend policy.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from dataclasses import dataclass
import importlib
import os


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class _Route:
    family: str | None
    owner: object
    admission: object = None
    primary_admission: object = None


class _FamilySelection:
    def __init__(self, name, bundle_module, control_module, bundle_selector,
                 control_selector, installed, control_admit,
                 primary_family='bundle', primary_admit=None):
        self.name = name
        self.bundle_module = bundle_module
        self.control_module = control_module
        self.bundle_selector = bundle_selector
        self.control_selector = control_selector
        self.installed = installed
        self.control_admit = control_admit
        self.primary_family = primary_family
        self.primary_admit = primary_admit
        self._unscoped = object()
        self._route = ContextVar(name + "_explicit_family", default=self._unscoped)

    def _modules(self):
        # All names above are fixed source literals, never manifest fields.
        return (importlib.import_module("." + self.bundle_module, __package__),
                importlib.import_module("." + self.control_module, __package__))

    def _captured(self, bundle, control):
        old = bundle._OWNER.get()
        new = control._OWNER.get()
        old_scoped = old is not bundle._UNSELECTED
        new_scoped = new is not control._UNSELECTED
        if not old_scoped and not new_scoped:
            return self._unscoped
        old_admission = old if old_scoped else None
        old_owner = (None if old_admission is None else old_admission.owner) if self.primary_admit else old_admission
        new_admission = new if new_scoped else None
        new_owner = None if new_admission is None else new_admission.owner
        if old_owner is not None and new_owner is not None:
            raise ValueError(self.name + " bundle and CONTROL scopes overlap")
        if old_owner is not None:
            return _Route(self.primary_family, old_owner, primary_admission=old_admission if self.primary_admit else None)
        if new_owner is not None:
            return _Route("control", new_owner, new_admission)
        return _Route(None, None)

    def _select(self, namespace):
        captured = self._route.get()
        if captured is not self._unscoped:
            return captured
        bundle, control = self._modules()
        captured = self._captured(bundle, control)
        if captured is not self._unscoped:
            return captured
        old_path = os.environ.get(self.bundle_selector)
        new_path = os.environ.get(self.control_selector)
        if old_path and new_path:
            raise ValueError(self.name + " requires one explicit native family")
        if old_path:
            if self.primary_admit:
                admitted = getattr(bundle, self.primary_admit)(old_path, namespace)
                return _Route(self.primary_family, admitted.owner, primary_admission=admitted)
            return _Route(self.primary_family, getattr(bundle, self.installed)(old_path, namespace))
        if new_path:
            admitted = getattr(control, self.control_admit)(new_path, namespace)
            return _Route("control", admitted.owner, admitted)
        return _Route(None, None)

    def selected(self, namespace):
        return self._select(namespace).owner

    def observe(self):
        """Return captured scope, family and owner without selecting or admitting."""
        captured = self._route.get()
        if captured is self._unscoped:
            captured = self._captured(*self._modules())
        if captured is self._unscoped:
            return False, None, None
        return True, captured.family, captured.owner

    def active(self):
        scoped, family, owner = self.observe()
        return family, owner

    @contextmanager
    def _bind(self, selected):
        bundle, control = self._modules()
        previous_route = self._route.get()
        previous_bundle = bundle._OWNER.get()
        previous_control = control._OWNER.get()
        try:
            # Record every prior value before set. Losing a set() return value
            # or an intermediate STORE cannot leak a selection after unwind.
            primary = selected.primary_admission if self.primary_admit else selected.owner
            bundle._OWNER.set(primary if selected.family == self.primary_family else None)
            control._OWNER.set(selected.admission if selected.family == "control" else None)
            self._route.set(selected)
            yield
        finally:
            try:
                self._route.set(previous_route)
            finally:
                try:
                    control._OWNER.set(previous_control)
                finally:
                    bundle._OWNER.set(previous_bundle)

    @contextmanager
    def scope(self, namespace):
        selected = self._select(namespace)
        with self._bind(selected):
            yield

    def identity(self, namespace):
        selected = self._select(namespace)
        if selected.owner is None:
            return b""
        bundle, control = self._modules()
        with self._bind(selected):
            if selected.family == self.primary_family:
                raw = bundle._bundle_implementation_identity(namespace)
            elif selected.family == "control":
                raw = control.native_implementation_identity(namespace)
            else:
                raise ValueError(self.name + " captured family is outside its inventory")
        return selected.family.encode("ascii") + b"\0" + raw

"""Fresh admission and whole-operation capture for the native Core emitter.
A captured absence is explicit; callbacks cannot replace the selected owner.
Each new operation independently admits its current manifest/source/image.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from dataclasses import dataclass
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from .hia_core_emitter_control_native import NativeCoreEmitter, SOURCE, SCHEMA, SELECTOR
from .hia_json_preflight_native import (
    MAX_IMAGE_BYTES, _installed_json_image, _unique_manifest_pairs)

_UNSELECTED = object()
_OWNER = ContextVar('hia_core_emitter_control_selected_owner', default=_UNSELECTED)
_OWNER_CACHE = []


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class _Admission:
    owner: NativeCoreEmitter
    checker_owner: object


def _bounded(path, maximum):
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        raw = stream.read(maximum + 1)
    if len(raw) > maximum:
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter input exceeds its private extent')
    return raw


def _manifest(raw):
    value = json.JSONDecoder(object_pairs_hook=_unique_manifest_pairs).decode(raw.decode('utf-8'))
    if (type(value) is not dict or set(value) != {
            'schema', 'source_sha256', 'image_path', 'image_sha256', 'compiler_sha256'}
            or value['schema'] != SCHEMA or type(value['image_path']) is not str
            or any(type(value[key]) is not str or len(value[key]) != 64
                   or any(c not in '0123456789abcdef' for c in value[key])
                   for key in ('source_sha256', 'image_sha256', 'compiler_sha256'))):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter manifest identity differs')
    return value


def _admit(manifest_path, namespace=None):
    """Freshly bind disk inputs and keep the admitted RX mapping immutable."""
    if namespace is None:
        from . import hia_program_native
        namespace = vars(hia_program_native)
    if type(namespace) is not dict:
        raise TypeError('native Core emitter requires an actual module namespace')
    path = Path(manifest_path).resolve(strict=True)
    raw = _bounded(path, 16384)
    manifest = _manifest(raw)
    source = SOURCE.read_bytes()
    image_path = (path.parent / manifest['image_path']).resolve(strict=True)
    image_raw = _bounded(image_path, MAX_IMAGE_BYTES)
    if (sha256(source).hexdigest() != manifest['source_sha256']
            or sha256(image_raw).hexdigest() != manifest['image_sha256']):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter source or image identity differs')
    loaded = _installed_json_image(str(path), SOURCE, SCHEMA, NativeCoreEmitter)
    if (loaded.admitted_source_sha256 != manifest['source_sha256']
            or loaded.image_sha256 != manifest['image_sha256']
            or _bounded(path, 16384) != raw or SOURCE.read_bytes() != source
            or _bounded(image_path, MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) != image_raw):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter admission inputs changed')
    owner = loaded if loaded.namespace is namespace else None
    if owner is None:
        for previous, previous_namespace, candidate in _OWNER_CACHE:
            if previous is loaded and previous_namespace is namespace:
                owner = candidate
                break
    if owner is None:
        # A namespace view shares only immutable code/table and the reentrant
        # exception-delivery mapping. Each call owns independent HIA arenas.
        owner = object.__new__(NativeCoreEmitter)
        owner.__dict__.update(loaded.__dict__)
        owner._bind_namespace(namespace)
        _OWNER_CACHE.append((loaded, namespace, owner))
        if len(_OWNER_CACHE) > 3:
            del _OWNER_CACHE[0]
    from .hia_checker_identity import hold_native_owner
    # Each admission retains its own exact record. A reused image must not
    # overwrite metadata belonging to a different already-captured selection.
    return _Admission(owner, hold_native_owner(SELECTOR, owner, raw, source))


def installed_core_emitter(manifest_path, namespace=None):
    return _admit(manifest_path, namespace).owner


def _selected_admission(namespace):
    captured = _OWNER.get()
    if captured is not _UNSELECTED:
        return captured
    path = os.environ.get(SELECTOR)
    return _admit(path, namespace) if path else None


def selected_core_emitter(namespace):
    admitted = _selected_admission(namespace)
    return None if admitted is None else admitted.owner


def active_core_emitter():
    admitted = _OWNER.get()
    return None if admitted is _UNSELECTED or admitted is None else admitted.owner


def captured_checker_owner():
    """Expose only the actual scope's capability, including captured absence."""
    admitted = _OWNER.get()
    if admitted is _UNSELECTED:
        return False, None
    return True, None if admitted is None else admitted.checker_owner


@contextmanager
def native_core_emitter_scope(namespace):
    admitted = _selected_admission(namespace)
    previous = _OWNER.get()
    try:
        # Save the prior value before set(): a lost STORE of its return token
        # must not leave the surrounding operation with a leaked selection.
        _OWNER.set(admitted)
        yield
    finally:
        _OWNER.set(previous)


def native_implementation_identity(namespace):
    owner = selected_core_emitter(namespace)
    if owner is None:
        return b''
    source_sha = sha256(SOURCE.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    if source_sha != owner.admitted_source_sha256:
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter source identity mismatch')
    return ('core-emitter-control-native-v1\0' + source_sha + '\0' + owner.image_sha256).encode('ascii')

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

UNIT_SCHEMA = 'hepta.hia.core-emitter-unit-native.v1'
ABI_SOURCE = 'docs/HIA_CORE_EMITTER_ABI.json'
_UNSELECTED = object()
_OWNER = ContextVar('hia_core_emitter_selected_owner', default=_UNSELECTED)
_OWNER_CACHE = []
_MODE_ARITIES = (
    ('_Emitter.__init__', 2), ('_Emitter.ordered_blocks', 2),
    ('_Emitter.label', 2), ('_Emitter.function_symbol', 2),
    ('_Emitter.wrapper', 2), ('_Emitter.render', 1),
)


def _json(raw):
    return json.JSONDecoder(object_pairs_hook=_unique_manifest_pairs).decode(raw.decode('utf-8'))


def _digest(value):
    return type(value) is str and len(value) == 64 and all(c in '0123456789abcdef' for c in value)


def checked_abi(raw):
    value = _json(raw)
    if (type(value) is not dict or set(value) != {
            'schema', 'protocol_magic', 'pool_magic', 'packet_bytes',
            'workspace_bytes', 'output_bytes', 'pool_bytes', 'literal_count',
            'units', 'modes'}
            or value['schema'] != 'hepta.hia.core-emitter-abi.v1'
            or type(value['protocol_magic']) is not int or value['protocol_magic'] != MAGIC
            or type(value['pool_magic']) is not int or value['pool_magic'] != POOL_MAGIC
            or type(value['packet_bytes']) is not int or value['packet_bytes'] != 128):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter ABI identity differs')
    for name, minimum in (('workspace_bytes', 1024), ('output_bytes', 128),
                          ('pool_bytes', 16), ('literal_count', 3)):
        if type(value[name]) is not int or not minimum <= value[name] <= 1048576:
            raise ValueError('native Core emitter ABI extent differs: ' + name)
    units = value['units']
    if (type(units) is not list or not units
            or any(type(name) is not str or name != 'core_emitter_' + format(i, '03d')
                   for i, name in enumerate(units))):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter unit inventory differs')
    expected_modes = {name: {'number': index, 'arity': arity}
                      for index, (name, arity) in enumerate(_MODE_ARITIES, 1)}
    modes = value['modes']
    if (type(modes) is not dict or set(modes) != set(expected_modes)
            or any(type(row) is not dict or set(row) != {'number', 'arity'}
                   or type(row['number']) is not int or type(row['arity']) is not int
                   for row in modes.values()) or modes != expected_modes):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter mode inventory differs')
    return value


def source_names(abi):
    return tuple('examples/hia_bootstrap/' + name + '.hepta'
                 for name in ('core_emitter_pool', *abi['units']))


def _bounded_manifest(path):
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        raw = stream.read(16385)
    if len(raw) > 16384:
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter manifest exceeds size limit')
    return raw


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class _BundleCustody:
    """Exact admitted inputs; image bytes are from the retained RX mappings."""
    bundle_path: str
    bundle_raw: bytes
    abi_path: str
    abi_raw: bytes
    units: tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Loaded:
    abi: dict
    names: tuple
    images: tuple
    abi_sha256: str
    source_hashes: tuple
    bundle_sha256: str
    custody: _BundleCustody | None = None


@lru_cache(maxsize=3)
def _load_bundle(path, raw, abi_raw, unit_inputs, abi_path):
    abi = checked_abi(abi_raw)
    bundle = _json(raw)
    names = ('core_emitter_pool', *abi['units'])
    expected_paths = {name: name + '/manifest.json' for name in names}
    if (type(bundle) is not dict or set(bundle) != {
            'schema', 'abi_sha256', 'compiler_sha256', 'unit_manifests'}
            or bundle['schema'] != SCHEMA
            or not _digest(bundle['abi_sha256'])
            or not _digest(bundle['compiler_sha256'])
            or type(bundle['unit_manifests']) is not dict
            or bundle['unit_manifests'] != expected_paths):
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter bundle manifest differs')
    abi_sha = sha256(abi_raw).hexdigest()
    if bundle['abi_sha256'] != abi_sha:
        raise ValueError('native Core emitter ABI source identity mismatch')
    if tuple(row[0] for row in unit_inputs) != names:

    """An object description is outside the admitted ELF64 profile."""


def _reference_name(value):
    if type(value) is not str or _NAME.fullmatch(value) is None:
        raise MachineObjectError("invalid ELF symbol name")
    return value


def _reference_exact_int(value, lower, upper):
    return type(value) is int and lower <= value < upper


def _reference_write_elf_object(code, symbols, relocations, *, text_alignment=16):
    """Encode one machine-code image as Linux x86-64 ET_REL.

    ``symbols`` is a list of ``{name, offset, size, global}`` records. Private
    implementation functions must have ``global=False``. ``relocations`` is a
    list of ``{offset, symbol, type: 4, addend: -4}`` records naming E8 rel32 call
    operands. Input order does not affect symbol or relocation table ordering.
    """
    if type(text_alignment) is not int or text_alignment not in {16, 32, 64}:
        raise MachineObjectError("unreviewed text section alignment")
    if type(code) is not bytes or not code or len(code) > MAX_OBJECT_BYTES:
        raise MachineObjectError("nonempty bounded immutable machine bytes required")
    if (type(symbols) is not list or not 1 <= len(symbols) < MAX_SYMBOLS
            or type(relocations) is not list or len(relocations) > len(code) // 5):
        raise MachineObjectError("invalid symbol or relocation inventory")
    names, definitions = set(), []
    for row in symbols:
        if type(row) is not dict or set(row) != {"name", "offset", "size", "global"}:
            raise MachineObjectError("invalid function symbol record")
        name = _name(row["name"])
        if (name in names or type(row["global"]) is not bool
                or not _exact_int(row["offset"], 0, len(code))
                or not _exact_int(row["size"], 1, len(code) + 1)
                or row["offset"] + row["size"] > len(code)):
            raise MachineObjectError("duplicate or out-of-range function symbol")
        names.add(name)
        definitions.append(dict(row))
    spans = sorted((row["offset"], row["offset"] + row["size"]) for row in definitions)
    if any(right[0] < left[1] for left, right in zip(spans, spans[1:])):
        raise MachineObjectError("function symbol ranges overlap")
    # A local function starts at a known instruction boundary. This writer is
    # not a disassembler and does not assert complete ISA validation.
    checked_relocations = []
    undefined = set()
    for row in relocations:
        if (type(row) is not dict or set(row) != {"offset", "symbol", "type", "addend"}
                or not _exact_int(row["offset"], 1, len(code) - 3)
                or type(row["type"]) is not int or row["type"] != 4
                or type(row["addend"]) is not int or row["addend"] != -4):
            raise MachineObjectError("only explicit PLT32 call relocations are supported")
        name = _name(row["symbol"])
        offset = row["offset"]
        if code[offset - 1] != 0xe8 or code[offset:offset + 4] != b"\0" * 4:
            raise MachineObjectError("call relocation does not point to an E8 placeholder")
        checked_relocations.append(dict(row))
        if name not in names:
            undefined.add(name)
    relocations = sorted(checked_relocations, key=lambda row: row["offset"])
    if any(right["offset"] - left["offset"] < 5
           for left, right in zip(relocations, relocations[1:])):
        raise MachineObjectError("duplicate or overlapping call relocations")
    if len(names) + len(undefined) + 2 > MAX_SYMBOLS:
        raise MachineObjectError("ELF symbol inventory exceeds limit")
    local = sorted((x for x in definitions if not x["global"]), key=lambda x: x["name"])
    public = sorted((x for x in definitions if x["global"]), key=lambda x: x["name"])
    string_table = bytearray(b"\0")
    name_offsets = {}
    for name in sorted(names | undefined):
        name_offsets[name] = len(string_table)
        string_table.extend(name.encode("ascii") + b"\0")
    symtab = bytearray(b"\0" * 24)
    # STT_SECTION local symbol for .text; first function index is 2.
    symtab.extend(struct.pack("<IBBHQQ", 0, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0))
    symbol_indexes = {}
    for row in local + public:
        symbol_indexes[row["name"]] = len(symtab) // 24
        info = (0x10 if row["global"] else 0) | 2  # STT_FUNC
        visibility = 0 if row["global"] else 2  # STV_HIDDEN
        symtab.extend(struct.pack("<IBBHQQ", name_offsets[row["name"]], info, visibility,
                                  1, row["offset"], row["size"]))
    first_global = 2 + len(local)
    for name in sorted(undefined):
        symbol_indexes[name] = len(symtab) // 24
        symtab.extend(struct.pack("<IBBHQQ", name_offsets[name], 0x10, 0, 0, 0, 0))
    rela = bytearray()
    for row in relocations:
        rela.extend(struct.pack("<QQq", row["offset"],
                                (symbol_indexes[row["symbol"]] << 32) | 4, -4))
    section_names = ("", ".text", ".rela.text", ".symtab", ".strtab", ".shstrtab", ".note.GNU-stack")
    shstrtab = bytearray(b"\0")
    section_name_offsets = {"": 0}
    for name in section_names[1:]:
        section_name_offsets[name] = len(shstrtab)
        shstrtab.extend(name.encode("ascii") + b"\0")
    # name, type, flags, alignment, entry size, link, info, bytes
    sections = [
        (".text", 1, 6, text_alignment, 0, 0, 0, code),
        (".rela.text", 4, 0, 8, 24, 3, 1, bytes(rela)),
        (".symtab", 2, 0, 8, 24, 4, first_global, bytes(symtab)),
        (".strtab", 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, bytes(string_table)),
        (".shstrtab", 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, bytes(shstrtab)),
        (".note.GNU-stack", 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, b""),
    ]
    image = bytearray(b"\0" * 64)
    headers = [b"\0" * 64]
    for name, typ, flags, alignment, entsize, link, info, content in sections:
        image.extend(b"\0" * (-len(image) % alignment))
        offset = len(image)
        image.extend(content)
        headers.append(struct.pack("<IIQQQQIIQQ", section_name_offsets[name], typ, flags,
                                   0, offset, len(content), link, info, alignment, entsize))
    image.extend(b"\0" * (-len(image) % 8))
    shoff = len(image)
    image.extend(b"".join(headers))
    if len(image) > MAX_OBJECT_BYTES:
        raise MachineObjectError("ELF object exceeds byte budget")
    ident = b"\x7fELF" + bytes([2, 1, 1, 0]) + b"\0" * 8
    image[:64] = struct.pack("<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH", ident, 1, 62, 1, 0, 0,
                             shoff, 0, 64, 0, 0, 64, len(headers), 5)
    return bytes(image)

Image selection, source identity and object primitive execution are hosted
mechanical boundaries. No machine-object policy is implemented here.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from .hia_machine_object_native import NativeMachineObject
from .hia_core_lowering_native import MAGIC, POOL_MAGIC
from .hia_json_preflight_native import (
    NativeHiaJsonImage, _load_manifest, _source_resource_path,
    _unique_manifest_pairs)

SELECTOR = 'HEPTA_HIA_MACHINE_OBJECT_MANIFEST'
SCHEMA = 'hepta.hia.machine-object-native.v1'
UNIT_SCHEMA = 'hepta.hia.machine-object-unit-native.v1'
ABI_SOURCE = 'docs/HIA_MACHINE_OBJECT_ABI.json'
_UNSELECTED = object()
_OWNER = ContextVar('hia_machine_object_selected_owner', default=_UNSELECTED)
_OWNER_CACHE = []
_MODE_ARITIES = (('_name', 1), ('_exact_int', 3), ('write_elf_object', 4), ('elf.callback.0', 1), ('elf.callback.1', 1), ('elf.callback.2', 1), ('elf.callback.3', 1), ('elf.callback.4', 1), ('elf.callback.5', 1), ('elf.callback.6', 1))


def _json(raw):
    return json.JSONDecoder(object_pairs_hook=_unique_manifest_pairs).decode(raw.decode('utf-8'))


def _digest(value):
    return type(value) is str and len(value) == 64 and all(c in '0123456789abcdef' for c in value)


def checked_abi(raw):
    value = _json(raw)
    if (type(value) is not dict or set(value) != {
            'schema', 'protocol_magic', 'pool_magic', 'packet_bytes',
            'workspace_bytes', 'output_bytes', 'pool_bytes', 'literal_count',
            'units', 'modes'}
            or value['schema'] != 'hepta.hia.machine-object-abi.v1'
            or type(value['protocol_magic']) is not int or value['protocol_magic'] != MAGIC
            or type(value['pool_magic']) is not int or value['pool_magic'] != POOL_MAGIC
            or type(value['packet_bytes']) is not int or value['packet_bytes'] != 128):
        raise ValueError('native machine-object ABI identity differs')
    for name, minimum in (('workspace_bytes', 1024), ('output_bytes', 128),
                          ('pool_bytes', 16), ('literal_count', 3)):
        if type(value[name]) is not int or not minimum <= value[name] <= 1048576:
            raise ValueError('native machine-object ABI extent differs: ' + name)
    units = value['units']
    if (type(units) is not list or not units
            or any(type(name) is not str or name != 'machine_object_' + format(i, '03d')
                   for i, name in enumerate(units))):
        raise ValueError('native machine-object unit inventory differs')
    expected_modes = {name: {'number': index, 'arity': arity}
                      for index, (name, arity) in enumerate(_MODE_ARITIES, 1)}
    modes = value['modes']
    if (type(modes) is not dict or set(modes) != set(expected_modes)
            or any(type(row) is not dict or set(row) != {'number', 'arity'}
                   or type(row['number']) is not int or type(row['arity']) is not int
                   for row in modes.values()) or modes != expected_modes):
        raise ValueError('native machine-object mode inventory differs')
    return value


def source_names(abi):
    return tuple('examples/hia_bootstrap/' + name + '.hepta'
                 for name in ('machine_object_pool', *abi['units']))


def _bounded_manifest(path):
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        raw = stream.read(16385)
    if len(raw) > 16384:
        raise ValueError('native machine-object manifest exceeds size limit')
    return raw


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class _BundleCustody:
    bundle_path: str
    bundle_raw: bytes
    abi_path: str
    abi_raw: bytes
    units: tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Loaded:
    abi: dict
    names: tuple
    images: tuple
    abi_sha256: str
    source_hashes: tuple
    bundle_sha256: str
    custody: _BundleCustody | None = None


@lru_cache(maxsize=3)
def _load_bundle(path, raw, abi_raw, unit_inputs, abi_path):
    abi = checked_abi(abi_raw)
    bundle = _json(raw)
    names = ('machine_object_pool', *abi['units'])
    expected_paths = {name: name + '/manifest.json' for name in names}
    if (type(bundle) is not dict or set(bundle) != {
            'schema', 'abi_sha256', 'compiler_sha256', 'unit_manifests'}
            or bundle['schema'] != SCHEMA
            or not _digest(bundle['abi_sha256'])
            or not _digest(bundle['compiler_sha256'])
            or type(bundle['unit_manifests']) is not dict
            or bundle['unit_manifests'] != expected_paths):
        raise ValueError('native machine-object bundle manifest differs')
    abi_sha = sha256(abi_raw).hexdigest()
    if bundle['abi_sha256'] != abi_sha:
        raise ValueError('native machine-object ABI source identity mismatch')
    if tuple(row[0] for row in unit_inputs) != names:
        raise ValueError('native machine-object complete image order differs')
    images, source_hashes, custody_units = [], [], []
    for name, unit_path, unit_raw, source_sha, source_path, source_raw in unit_inputs:
        unit = _json(unit_raw)
        if type(unit) is not dict or unit.get('compiler_sha256') != bundle['compiler_sha256']:
            raise ValueError('native machine-object compiler identity differs across units')
        image = _load_manifest(unit_path, unit_raw, source_sha, UNIT_SCHEMA, NativeHiaJsonImage)
        images.append(image)
        source_hashes.append((name, source_sha))
        custody_units.append((name, source_path, source_raw, unit_path, unit_raw,
                              str(Path(unit_path).parent / unit['image_path']),
                              image._mapping[:]))
    return _Loaded(abi, tuple(names), tuple(images), abi_sha,
                   tuple(source_hashes), sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
                   _BundleCustody(path, raw, abi_path, abi_raw, tuple(custody_units)))


def installed_machine_object(manifest_path, namespace):
    """Re-admit all package sources and manifests; pin immutable mapped code.

    Disk image mutation does not replace an existing mapping with an unchanged
    cache key. A new unit manifest key forces fresh image admission. Source and
    ABI bytes are read on every selection, including a warm loaded bundle.
    """
    from .hia_native_helpers import check_native_scheduling_scope, pinned_scheduling
    captured = pinned_scheduling(manifest_path, 'machine-object', namespace)
    if captured is not None:
        return captured
    check_native_scheduling_scope()
    if type(namespace) is not dict:
        raise TypeError('native machine-object requires an actual module namespace')
    path = Path(manifest_path).resolve(strict=True)
    raw = _bounded_manifest(path)
    abi_path = _source_resource_path(ABI_SOURCE)
    abi_raw = abi_path.read_bytes()
    abi = checked_abi(abi_raw)
    # Do not follow manifest-controlled paths before admitting its fixed shape.
    bundle = _json(raw)
    if type(bundle) is dict and bundle.get('schema')=='hepta.hia.native-continuation-inprocess.v1':
        from .hia_native_continuation_selection import installed_native_continuation
        return installed_native_continuation(path,namespace,kind='machine-object')
    names = ('machine_object_pool', *abi['units'])
    paths = {name: name + '/manifest.json' for name in names}
    if (type(bundle) is not dict or set(bundle) != {
            'schema', 'abi_sha256', 'compiler_sha256', 'unit_manifests'}
            or bundle.get('schema') != SCHEMA
            or not _digest(bundle.get('abi_sha256'))
            or not _digest(bundle.get('compiler_sha256'))
            or bundle.get('unit_manifests') != paths
            or bundle['abi_sha256'] != sha256(abi_raw).hexdigest()):
        raise ValueError('native machine-object bundle or ABI source identity differs')
    inputs = []
    for name in names:
        unit_path = (path.parent / paths[name]).resolve(strict=True)
        unit_raw = _bounded_manifest(unit_path)
        relative = 'examples/hia_bootstrap/' + name + '.hepta'
        source_path = _source_resource_path(relative)
        source_raw = source_path.read_bytes()
        inputs.append((name, str(unit_path), unit_raw,
                       sha256(source_raw).hexdigest(), str(source_path), source_raw))
    loaded = _load_bundle(str(path), raw, abi_raw, tuple(inputs), str(abi_path))
    for previous_loaded, previous_namespace, owner in _OWNER_CACHE:
        if previous_loaded is loaded and previous_namespace is namespace:
            return owner
    owner = NativeMachineObject(loaded.images[1:], loaded.images[0], loaded.abi, namespace)
    owner._admitted_bundle = loaded
    _OWNER_CACHE.append((loaded, namespace, owner))
    if len(_OWNER_CACHE) > 3:
        del _OWNER_CACHE[0]
    return owner


def selected_machine_object(namespace):
    owner = _OWNER.get()
    if owner is not _UNSELECTED:
        return owner
    path = os.environ.get(SELECTOR)
    return installed_machine_object(path, namespace) if path else None


def active_machine_object():
    """Helpers outside an admitted ordinary emit retain their original entry."""
    owner = _OWNER.get()
    return None if owner is _UNSELECTED else owner


@contextmanager
def native_machine_object_scope(namespace):
    owner = selected_machine_object(namespace)
    token = _OWNER.set(owner)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _OWNER.reset(token)


def native_implementation_identity(namespace):
    owner = selected_machine_object(namespace)
    if owner is None:
        return b''
    loaded = owner._admitted_bundle
    abi_sha = sha256(_source_resource_path(ABI_SOURCE).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    if abi_sha != loaded.abi_sha256:
        raise ValueError('native machine-object ABI source identity mismatch')
    expected_sources = dict(loaded.source_hashes)
    values = ['native-machine-object-v1', abi_sha, loaded.bundle_sha256]
    for name, image in zip(loaded.names, loaded.images):
        relative = 'examples/hia_bootstrap/' + name + '.hepta'
        source_sha = sha256(_source_resource_path(relative).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if source_sha != expected_sources[name]:
            raise ValueError('native machine-object source identity mismatch')
        values.extend((relative, source_sha, image.image_sha256))
    continuation=getattr(owner,'_native_continuation_identity',b'')
    if continuation:values.append(continuation.hex())
    return ('\0'.join(values)).encode('ascii')


def captured_selected_owner():
    owner = _OWNER.get()
    return (False, None) if owner is _UNSELECTED else (True, owner)


def _bundle_implementation_identity(namespace):
    return native_implementation_identity(namespace)

    NativeHiaJsonImage, _installed_json_image, _source_resource_path)

SOURCE = _source_resource_path('examples/hia_bootstrap/machine_plan.hepta')
SCHEMA = 'hepta.hia.machine-plan-native.v1'
SELECTOR = 'HEPTA_HIA_MACHINE_PLAN_MANIFEST'

REGISTERS = ('rbx', 'r12', 'r13', 'r14', 'r15', 'r8', 'r9')
LEAF_OPS = tuple(sorted((
    'const', 'int.add.wrap', 'int.add.checked', 'int.sub.wrap', 'int.sub.checked',
    'int.mul.wrap', 'int.mul.checked', 'int.div.checked', 'int.rem.checked',
    'int.shl.checked', 'int.shr.checked', 'int.neg.checked', 'int.cast',
    'bit.and', 'bit.or', 'bit.xor', 'bit.not', 'compare.eq', 'compare.ne',
    'compare.lt', 'compare.le', 'compare.gt', 'compare.ge', 'bool.and',
    'bool.or', 'bool.not', 'select', 'buffer.len', 'buffer.load', 'buffer.store')))
RULE = 'closed-block inclusive lifetimes; all edge sources staged before target writes'
MESSAGES = {
    1: 'plan must be an object',
    2: 'plan requires bounded plain JSON data',
    3: 'unknown plan schema',
    4: 'plan has missing or unreviewed fields',
    5: 'plan belongs to a different Core',
    6: 'invalid block order map',
    7: 'unknown function in block order',
    8: 'block order must name every member exactly once',
    9: 'function order must name every member exactly once',
    10: 'scratch assignment must bijectively rename only r10 and r11',
    11: 'instruction choices must be explicit and complete',
    12: 'unreviewed immediate move encoding',
    13: 'unreviewed immediate arithmetic encoding',
    14: 'unreviewed function alignment',
    15: 'unreviewed scalar select encoding',
    16: 'value_registers must be a function map',
    17: 'unknown function in value register assignment',
    18: 'value registers must be explicit assignments admitted by this plan version',
    19: 'caller-clobbered value registers require a leaf opcode whitelist; no calls, swap or allocation/bulk helpers',
